name: Kontra (Ristikontra)
description: Kontra (primarily known as Ristikontra) is an unusual Finnish trick-taking game popular in lumber camps and traditional social clubs. Played by four players in two fixed partnerships, it features a unique trick-capture rule: tricks are won by the player who plays the *last* card of the same rank as the card that led the trick. It is a game of timing and point-counting rather than suit-power.

overview.description: Kontra (primarily known as Ristikontra) is an unusual Finnish trick-taking game popular in lumber camps and traditional social clubs. Played by four players in two fixed partnerships, it features a unique trick-capture rule: tricks are won by the player who plays the *last* card of the same rank as the card that led the trick. It is a game of timing and point-counting rather than suit-power.

history.origins: Developed in early 20th-century Finland among foresters and rural workers. The 'Risti' (Cross) in Ristikontra refers to the partnership structure. The game's mechanics focus on efficiency and waste-reduction, reflecting its humble origins.
timeline: 1920s: Gaining popularity in Eastern Finland lumber camps.
1950s: Rules codified in Finnish card manuals.
Present: A niche traditional game, often revived in regional cultural festivals.
history.cultural: Commonly played as a game of 'quiet calculation'â€”partners must coordinate without speaking, watching their timing above all else.
history.evolution: The game evolved to have a very specific Ace-Ten scoring system which is common across North-Eastern Europe but applied here to an erratic 'Last-Equal-Card' capture rule.

setup.players: 4 players in fixed partnerships (North-South vs East-West).
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Suits and standard Ranks (A-K) are used, but suit power is irrelevant for capturing.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 6 cards. The remaining cards form a stock pile.

rules.objective: Win tricks containing point-scoring cards (Aces, 10s, Kings, Queens, Jacks). Total points available: 120.
rules.gameplay:
1. Must play one card per trick.
2. After each trick, players draw from the stock to return to 6 cards.
3. There is NO follow-suit requirement.
4. When the stock is empty, players play out the remaining cards in hand.
keyRules: Trick won by the last card of the same rank as the card led; no follow-suit requirement.
After each trick, players draw from the stock to restore six cards; winner draws first.
When stock is empty, the last six tricks are played without replenishment.
Cannot lead the same rank to four consecutive tricks.
61 or more card points wins the deal; 120 points scores two game points.

strategy.basic: Timing is everything. If the lead is a 10 (high points), and you are the 2nd player holding another 10, don't play it! If you do, the 3rd or 4th player could play their 10 and take the points. Wait until you are the last player.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Sacrificial Lead': Lead a card you have a double of (e.g., you have two 8s). If no one else plays an 8, you win. If they do, you can play your second 8 to potentially become the 'last equal card' played.
strategy.advanced: Card Counting: Keep track of which ranks have been fully played (four cards each). If 3 sevens have been played, and you hold the fourth, leading it guarantees you the trick because no one can 'last-match' you.
tips: The Ace is the most dangerous card to lead. It is worth 11 points, and if another player matches it, they get all 11 points effortlessly.
Save your low-point matching cards (e.g., 2s) to capture high-point cards that were led (like Aces).

variations.name: Zero points lose all
variations.description: If a team gets no points during a deal, they lose all points won in previous games; cumulative score drops to zero.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Scoring penalty only; no engine constant overrides needed for this variant.

variations.name: First to 120 cumulative
variations.description: Each team scores card points; first team to reach 120 cumulative points wins. Tie at 120: team that did not win the last trick containing a counting card wins.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Standard target scoring; engine uses default targetScore from main game.

variations.name: Alternative card values (60 points)
variations.description: Ace=5, king=4, queen=3, jack=2, ten=1; 60 points in pack. Team needs at least 31 to win; 30-30 holds game point in abeyance.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Card values and target differ; overrides to be added when implementing this variant.

scoring.description: Ace-Ten point count in tricks: A=11, 10=10, K=4, Q=3, J=2; 120 total. Team with more than half wins the deal.
scoring.winCondition: Partnership with more than half the card points (61 or more) wins the deal and scores 1 game point; 120 points scores 2. First team to reach agreed target (usually 7) wins the game.
